intro: Every tool the modeling assistant can call, with what it needs, what it returns, a worked example and a visual drawn from that example. The examples are checked against the code by the backend test suite, so they stay accurate as the tools change.
rules: Only applying a proposal changes the scene: editor.apply_proposal, or editor.propose_commands and modeling.propose_generated with apply true, which run the same apply step in the same call. Every other tool reads, calculates, plans or stores.
A calculated batch is strict. Pass expectedRevision; if the scene changes first, the proposal fails and must be made again rather than moved onto the new scene.
A failed tool returns { "error": "...", "details": ... } to the model, so it can correct the call. The run keeps going.

Arguments that do not match a tool's schema come back as { "error", "issues" }: each issue has a path such as commands[1] (commandId "lid").transform.scale and what is wrong there, and an unknown command type lists the closest valid ones.

editor.plan_placement, editor.plan_duplicates and modeling.generate_commands return a planId. editor.propose_commands accepts it in place of commands, so generated commands and ids are never copied by hand.

conventions.meaning: Match [A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}. Object and collection ids are separate.
Nonnegative integers. Every read reports one, and calculated or proposed batches refer back to it.
Name a mesh inside an imported object. Each step is a part name (Arm), a repeat (Arm#1 is the second one) or a child index. Use the paths the inspection returns.
[x, y, z] in scene units. Positions are local to the parent unless a tool says world.
Scene units unless the project is calibrated; then measurementUnits says how many meters one scene unit is.

types.label: Read
types.hint: These tools look at the scene or calculate a result. Nothing changes.

types.label: Plan
types.hint: Records intent and the steps for a task. It changes nothing.

types.label: Propose
types.hint: Stores a batch of changes for review. The scene is still unchanged.

types.label: Apply
types.hint: Changes the scene by applying a stored proposal.

types.label: Skill
types.hint: Loads the workflow for a skill selected for this request.

tools.name: editor.get_context
tools.summary: Reads the whole scene: every object with its parent and transform, the selection, the revision, and which features the editor supports.
when: First step of any change. It is the only way to learn object ids and the current revision.
Again when a proposal may have been overtaken by a change.

input.note: No input. Send an empty object.

rows.meaning: The scene revision. Pass it as expectedRevision or sourceRevision.
id, name, type, parentId, transform, visible, collectionId and worldBounds for each object.
Objects the user has selected.
Object or Edit mode, and in Edit mode the components the user has picked.
Which command families this editor accepts.

flow: Assistant calls editor.get_context
Editor sends a snapshot for this client
Assistant uses the ids and revision in its next call

visual.caption: The sample scene at revision 12. Indentation is the parent relation.

tips: Use editor.get_scene_summary when only counts are needed; this result can be large. On a large scene read by branch with editor.read_branch, or select with editor.query_objects, and keep this for the exact transforms of objects already chosen.
worldBounds includes descendants and hidden geometry. It uses geometry bounding boxes, not evaluated shapes.
limits: A snapshot holds up to 2000 objects.
It does not evaluate geometry. Use editor.measure or editor.inspect_mesh for shape.

tools.name: editor.get_scene_summary
tools.summary: Counts the objects by type and reports what is selected. A quick orientation before a larger read.
when: When the assistant needs the size and shape of the scene without the full object list.
Before choosing how to read a large scene: with more than about 60 objects, continue with editor.read_branch.

input.note: No input. Send an empty object.

rows.meaning: The scene revision.
The open scene's name, or null.
Total objects.
How many objects of each type. Only types that occur are listed.
The selected object ids.

visual.caption: Counts by type for the sample scene.

tips: It reports counts and selection only. For parents, transforms or names, use editor.get_context.
limits: No positions, names or parents in the result.

tools.name: editor.read_branch
tools.summary: Reads the scene as a tree, one branch at a time. Each entry carries a summary, and runs of look-alike siblings fold into one entry, so the answer grows with what the scene contains, not with its object count.
when: First, on any scene with more than about 60 objects, instead of reading the whole flat list.
To find the id of a part by its place in the hierarchy.
To see how big a group is and what it holds before deciding to open it.

input.note: Every field is optional. Send {} for the top level.

rows.name: rootId
rows.meaning: The object to open. Leave out for the top of the scene.

rows.name: depth
rows.meaning: How many levels to open below the root. A level that stays closed shows only counts.

rows.name: childLimit
rows.meaning: Entries listed per level.

rows.name: childOffset
rows.meaning: Entries to skip at the opened level, for paging. Use the nextOffset a result gives.

rows.name: foldRepeats
rows.meaning: Shows 4 or more look-alike siblings as one entry. Set false to list every sibling.
The scene revision, and the number of objects in the whole scene.
Objects by type, for the whole scene. Only when no rootId is given.
The opened object: id, name, type, visible, size and center in world axes, childCount, descendantCount and descendants by type. Not present at the top level.
The id and name of each object from the top of the scene down to the opened one.

The entries of the level, each with the same summary and, when depth allows, its own children and childrenOmitted. A folded run is { repeat: true, name, type, count, templateId, exampleIds, size, descendantsEach }.
Entries not returned at the opened level, and the childOffset that continues the listing.
True when the read stopped opening branches at its limit of 300 entries.
Objects left out because their parents form a cycle. Present only when there are some.

visual.caption: The sample scene's hierarchy. Reading Figure lists Torso and the two Arms with sizes and counts.

tips: Open a branch only when you need it. A folded entry stands for many objects; its templateId is one of them.
size and center are world-space and include what is inside the object, so a group's size is the size of the whole assembly.
Use editor.get_context for exact transforms of objects you have already chosen, not to find them.
limits: One read returns at most 300 entries, and a level at most childLimit.
Folding compares type, name (ignoring numbering), size and contents, not geometry.

errors.message: rootId "…" is not in the scene; read the scene with editor.read_branch to find the id
errors.cause: rootId names no object, or an object caught in a parent cycle.

tools.name: editor.find_repeats
tools.summary: Finds objects that look like copies of one another and says how they are laid out, so a repeated part is one idea to change instead of many objects.
when: Before editing a scene with many similar parts, such as windows, posts, tiles or rivets.
To learn the spacing of an array so it can be reproduced with editor.plan_duplicates.
To spot copies that were piled in one place by mistake.

rows.name: rootId
rows.meaning: Search only below this object. Leave out to search the whole scene.

rows.name: minCount
rows.meaning: The smallest number of look-alikes that counts as a group.

rows.name: limit
rows.meaning: Groups returned, the ones standing for most of the scene first.
The scene revision.
Objects looked at, and objects inside the groups returned, members and what they hold.
The shared name without its numbering, the type, and the number of members.
The member to treat as the original, and the first 50 member ids. memberIdsOmitted counts the rest.
World size of one member, and how many objects each holds.
Up to five distinct parents, and how many there are.
line { axis, count, step }, grid { axes, counts, steps }, coincident (all in one place) or scattered, from the members' world centers.
Groups that matched but are past the limit.
A reminder that matching used names, sizes and structure, not geometry.

response.confidence: Matched by type, name, size and contents; geometry is not compared.

visual.caption: Top view. The two Arms match: the same size, name and kind, 1.8 apart along x.

tips: A repeated group is reported once; the frames and panes inside repeated windows are not listed again.
A line or grid maps onto editor.plan_duplicates: sourceId is templateId, offset is the step on the axis.
Confirm with editor.inspect_mesh on templateId and one other member before treating them as identical.
limits: Matches by type, name (ignoring trailing numbers and "copy"), world size to about 3 significant digits and contents. Geometry and materials are not compared.
Copies turned by other than a quarter turn, or scaled differently, are not matched.
Objects with no bounds cannot be compared and are skipped.

errors.message: rootId "…" is not in the scene; read the scene with editor.read_branch to find the id
errors.cause: rootId names no object.

tools.name: editor.query_objects
tools.summary: Selects objects by rule, such as name, type, parent, size or position, so a group of objects can be named by what they are instead of by id.
when: To find every object of a kind, for example all windows above the second floor.
To count objects before and after an edit.
To get the ids for one batch of commands without reading the whole scene.

input.note: Every field is optional, and every filter given must hold.

rows.name: nameMatches
rows.meaning: A pattern for the object's own name. * is any run of characters, ? is one; case is ignored.

rows.name: type
rows.type: list of mesh | empty | collection | camera | light
rows.meaning: Keep only these types.

rows.name: parentId
rows.meaning: Direct children of this object. null selects the top level.

rows.name: withinId
rows.meaning: Everything below this object, at any depth.

rows.name: visible, selected
rows.meaning: Filter on the object's own visibility flag, or on whether it is selected.

rows.name: size
rows.type: { x?, y?, z? } of { min?, max? }
rows.meaning: Ranges on the world extents, including what is inside. Objects with no geometry never match.

rows.name: position
rows.type: { x?, y?, z? } of { min?, max? }
rows.meaning: Ranges on the world center of the object's bounds. Objects with no geometry never match.

rows.name: sortBy
rows.type: scene | name | size | x | y | z
rows.meaning: size orders by volume; x, y and z by the center on that axis.

rows.name: descending
rows.meaning: Reverse the order.

rows.name: limit, offset
rows.meaning: Page the matches.

rows.name: countOnly
rows.meaning: Return only the total.
The scene revision the matches belong to.
Every object that matched, whatever the limit.
The page of matches: id, name, type, parentId, size and center (world axes).
Whether more matches follow, and the offset that continues.

visual.caption: Objects of the sample scene against nameMatches "arm*" and a center at x ≤ 0.

tips: Matches describe the scene at the revision returned. After an edit, query again.
Combine withinId with a name pattern to select one kind of part inside one branch.
Use countOnly to check an edit worked without reading the objects.
limits: At most 200 matches per call; page with offset.
size and position use the editor's world bounds, which include descendants.

errors.message: withinId "…" is not in the scene; read the scene with editor.read_branch to find the id
errors.cause: withinId or parentId names no object.

tools.name: editor.describe_commands
tools.summary: Returns the full rules of the editor commands asked for: fields, limits, batching and what each refuses. editor.propose_commands lists every command in one line, so the details are read only when needed.
when: Before the first geometry or material command of a kind in a run.
When a proposal was refused and the issue does not make the fix clear.

rows.name: types
rows.meaning: Command types such as geometry.bisect. Repeats are answered once.
For each known type: type, summary (the line editor.propose_commands shows) and rules.
Types that are not commands, each with the three closest valid types.

commands.summary: Reverses whole connected surfaces: omit ids for all, or list base faces and each surface containing one flips.
commands.rules: IDs are unchanged, so it can share a component-edit batch.

visual.caption: One known command and one misspelled type.

tips: Ask for every type a batch will use in one call.
The command list in editor.propose_commands and these rules come from the same table, so they always agree.
limits: Reads nothing from the scene; use editor.inspect_mesh or editor.get_context for ids and revisions.
At most 12 types per call.

tools.name: editor.inspect_mesh
tools.summary: Reads the topology of one mesh: vertices, edges and faces, the faces that match a direction or position query, and its bounds.
when: Before any geometry change, so the change uses real ids.
To answer questions such as which faces point up, or whether a mesh is closed.

input.note: The request is validated by meshInspectionRequestSchema.

rows.name: objectId
rows.meaning: The object to inspect.

rows.name: meshPath
rows.meaning: A mesh inside the object. [] is the object itself.

rows.name: view
rows.meaning: base reads the unmodified cage that edits change; evaluated reads the displayed mesh.

rows.name: offset
rows.meaning: Page offset for the vertex, edge and face samples.

rows.name: limit
rows.meaning: Samples per page.

rows.name: includeSamples
rows.meaning: false omits the vertex, edge and face pages.

rows.name: materialsOnly
rows.meaning: true reads materials without topology.

rows.name: faceQuery
rows.meaning: Filters faces. Needs normal, or a centerMin/centerMax bound.

rows.name: openings
rows.meaning: Lists the openings (closed chains of boundary edges) with their edge IDs, ready for fill_hole or bridge_edge_loops. Optional offset and limit (1–50, default 20).

rows.name: shells
rows.meaning: Lists the connected parts, each with a face that names it, its size and its extent. Optional offset and limit (1–50, default 20).
The scene revision, and why the inspection is unavailable when it is.
ok, unsupported or not_found.
vertices (welded), renderVertices, edges, faces (polygons), triangles, boundaryEdges, nonManifoldEdges, inconsistentEdges, materialSlots.
Bounds in mesh space, and the matrix that places the mesh in the scene.
One page of samples. Indices refer to the whole mesh, not to the page.
ids of matching faces on this page, with total, offset and hasMore.

loops: for each opening its edges (canonical IDs in walking order, at most 256), edgeCount, truncated, and its center, min and max. Also total, offset, hasMore, and irregularEdges for boundary edges that are not in a simple closed loop.
shells: for each connected part its faceCount, firstFace (a face ID that names the whole part), closed (it encloses a volume), center, min and max. Also total, offset and hasMore.

rows.label: normal
rows.meaning: A nonzero direction in mesh-local space.

rows.label: minDot
rows.meaning: How closely a face must point along normal, from -1 to 1. The description's default is 0.9.

rows.label: centerMin, centerMax
rows.meaning: Local bounds that a face's centre must lie inside.

rows.label: offset, limit
rows.meaning: Paging for matches. limit is 1–1000, default 100.

flow: Assistant asks for the base or evaluated mesh
Editor returns stats and one page of samples
Face ids are used with the same view and revision in the next call

visual.caption: Isometric view of the crate. Matched: face 5 (+Y, minDot 0.95).

tips: Inspect the base view before editing: geometry edits change the base cage.
faceMatches holds ids, not positions. Read hasMore before relying on a page.
limits: Meshes above about 20,000 triangles may be unsupported.
Inspection reports geometry counts. It does not judge appearance; use viewport.capture for that.

tools.name: editor.inspect_materials
tools.summary: Reads the material slots of one object: name, shader, colour, roughness, metalness, opacity, sidedness and texture channels, without reading topology.
when: Before any material proposal. The slot indices and revision it returns are what material commands use.

rows.name: objectId
rows.meaning: The object whose materials to read.

rows.name: meshPath
rows.meaning: A mesh inside the object.

rows.name: offset
rows.meaning: First slot to return.

rows.name: limit
rows.meaning: Slots per page.
Use as expectedRevision for material commands.
ok, unsupported or not_found, and the reason.
Total slots on this mesh, across all pages.
slot, name, type, editable, color, emissive, roughness, metalness, opacity, transparent, depthWrite, side, textures.
For a group, the mesh paths available inside it.

tips: Standard and Physical materials are editable. Other shaders need material.replace_slot, which discards their maps and settings. Do not replace a shader just to change a colour.
limits: Texture channels are named, not exposed. Creating or importing textures is not available.

tools.name: viewport.capture
tools.summary: Lets the assistant look at the scene. The editor draws it from one to six views and returns the pictures, with where each object sits in each one.
when: To check shapes, proportions, placement and surface problems that numbers cannot show.
Before applying a proposal, by passing its proposalId.

rows.name: views
rows.meaning: Each view places the camera by preset, orbit or exact camera, with optional label, projection and zoom.

rows.name: proposalId
rows.meaning: Draw this pending proposal from the run as an isolated copy.

rows.name: focus, highlight
rows.meaning: Objects to frame and report bounds for; objects to box in orange.

rows.name: isolate
rows.meaning: Draw only the focused objects.

rows.name: mode
rows.meaning: normals shows flipped or faceted faces.

rows.name: labels, guides
rows.meaning: Object ids on the picture; a floor grid and axes.

rows.name: width, height
rows.meaning: Image size in pixels.
The result status, the axis conventions, and how to read the measurements.
Object count and the bounds of everything.
For each focused object: bounds, size and center.
label, size, camera used, and each listed object's screenBounds and inFrame.
Present when a proposal was drawn.

details.title: Camera placement, in order of priority

rows.label: camera
rows.meaning: Exact position, target and optional fov, in world space.

rows.label: orbit
rows.meaning: azimuthDegrees and elevationDegrees around the framed objects. Azimuth 0 looks at the front from +Z.

rows.label: preset
rows.meaning: front, back, left, right, top, bottom, isometric (default), or current for the user's own camera.

response.coordinates: Y is up. A front view looks along -Z (it sees the +Z side), a right view looks along -X, a left view looks along +X, a back view looks along +Z.
response.note: The images follow in the order of views. screenBounds is each object's projected bounding box in pixels, not a visibility test.

flow: Assistant chooses views and what to focus on
Editor draws offscreen and returns a JPEG per view with measurements
Model reads the measurements, then the pictures, and states its conclusion in its reply

visual.caption: Projected boxes from screenBounds. They show where objects are, not whether they are visible.

tips: Start with overview views, then focus and zoom into anything suspicious.
Pass proposalId to check a stored proposal before it is applied.
limits: Up to six views per call; each JPEG stays under about 1.5 MB.
The call times out after EDITOR_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS (15 seconds by default).

An OpenAI-compatible endpoint receives the pictures in the message after the tool result, for the latest four captures; earlier ones keep their measurements. Turn Send pictures off in the provider settings for a model that cannot read images, and the assistant gets measurements only.
The editor window keeps the last 12 captures. Pictures are not kept in the saved conversation.

tools.name: validation.check_scene
tools.summary: Checks the scene for structural problems and reports each with a severity: errors, warnings and information.
when: As the last step of a change, after the proposal is applied. The mesh-editing and character-modeling skills both do this.
When the user asks whether the scene is in order.
limits: The run keeps asking the assistant to carry on until a check follows the last change and reports no errors, up to three times per request. A plan step that names a stepId must also have an applied batch.

input.note: No input. Send an empty object.

rows.meaning: false only when there is at least one error.
Objects in the snapshot.
severity, objectId (null for a collection or scene-wide issue) and message.

rows.label: error · ids and parents
rows.meaning: Duplicate object ids; a parent that does not exist; a parent chain that loops.

rows.label: error · scale
rows.meaning: A scale that is zero or negative on any axis.

rows.label: error · collections
rows.meaning: A collection in a missing collection or inside itself; an object in a missing collection.

rows.label: warning · names
rows.meaning: Two objects with the same name under one parent (the later one is reported); two collections with the same name in one place.

rows.label: warning · structure
rows.meaning: A group with children scaled by different amounts on different axes, and a selected id that is not in the scene.

rows.label: warning · size
rows.meaning: More than 500 objects, where checks may be slow to review.

rows.label: info
rows.meaning: A group with no children, or a collection with nothing in it.

issues.message: Shares the name "Arm" with another object under the same parent; rename one so each can be told apart

visual.caption: Result for the sample scene: no errors, one warning, one note.

issues.message: Shares the name "Arm" with another object under the same parent

tips: A warning does not stop an edit. But a later move under or out of an unevenly scaled group is refused, so fix that warning first.
limits: It reads the snapshot only. It cannot find self-intersections or overlaps; use editor.measure or viewport.capture for those.

tools.name: editor.measure
tools.summary: Measures the geometry the editor shows: size, distance, angle, edge length or the clearance between two objects, from evaluated geometry.
when: When the user asks how big something is, how far apart two things are, or whether two objects touch.
To confirm a placement after it has been applied.

rows.name: request
rows.meaning: One of five kinds, selected by request.kind (see the table).

rows.label: dimensions
rows.meaning: target {objectId, meshPath?, descendants?} and space (world default, or local). Returns bounds, size, center.

rows.label: distance
rows.meaning: from and to, each a point or a vertex reference {objectId, vertex, revision}. Returns delta and length.

rows.label: edge
rows.meaning: objectId, revision and an edge id a_b. Returns endpoints and length.

rows.label: angle
rows.meaning: from, at and to. Returns degrees at the middle point.

rows.label: clearance
rows.meaning: first and second targets, method bounds (axis gaps) or surface (closest boundary distance). Returns distance and axisGap.
The scene revision. Use it for placement proposals.
null, or the display unit and metersPerSceneUnit.
{ status: ok, data } or { status: unavailable, message } with the reason.

visual.caption: Top view: x across, z toward the bottom. The gap between the torso and the crate is 2.

tips: Measure again after applying a placement, particularly when a Boolean changes the shape.
Use surface clearance to find touching or intersecting objects. Bounds clearance only gives axis gaps.
limits: Surface clearance is limited to 20,000 triangles per target and a bounded amount of work.
Skinned and morph-deformed meshes allow dimensions, but not component references.
Lengths are scene units unless the project is calibrated.

tools.name: editor.plan_placement
tools.summary: Works out the moves that align, space or snap objects, using the world bounds of evaluated geometry. It returns scene.move_object commands and changes nothing.
when: When a placement must be exact: put the crate on the floor, leave a 20 mm gap, space four posts evenly.
Typing coordinates by hand misses bounds and parents. This tool does not.

rows.name: request
rows.meaning: One of four operations, selected by request.kind (see the table).

rows.label: align
rows.meaning: objectIds (1–50), referenceId, axes (x, y, z), sourceAnchor and referenceAnchor (min, center or max). Matches bounds or centres.

rows.label: gap
rows.meaning: objectIds, referenceId, axis, side (positive or negative), a signed gap, and unit (scene, mm, cm, m, in or ft). Physical units need calibration.

rows.label: distribute
rows.meaning: At least three objectIds in increasing order on one axis. The endpoints stay put; mode gaps or centers spaces the rest.

rows.label: snap
rows.meaning: Exactly one object, world points from and to, and expectedRevision. Moves from onto to.
Propose the commands with this as expectedRevision.
scene.move_object commands, each with a delta in the parent's axes. Empty when nothing needs to move.
planned, or already_placed.
Pass it to editor.propose_commands instead of the commands. Left out when nothing needs to move.
The next step: propose by planId with apply true, then measure again.

response.nextAction: Call editor.propose_commands with this planId and apply true, then re-measure the result.

flow: Read the bounds at sourceRevision
Work out the wanted position for each object
Convert it to each parent's axes
Propose by planId with apply true, then measure

visual.caption: Side view: x across, y up. The crate rises 0.25 so its bottom matches the torso's.

tips: Use align with min anchors to put objects on a shared floor.
Bounds placement does not guarantee contact or the absence of collisions. Measure again afterwards.
limits: A physical gap needs a calibrated project.
Distribute fails when the endpoints leave too little room for non-overlapping gaps.

errors.message: Scene changed; inspect the points again
errors.cause: snap was planned against an older expectedRevision.

errors.message: Calibrate project units before physical placement
errors.cause: A gap used mm, cm, m, in or ft without a calibration.

errors.message: Placement targets cannot contain ancestors and descendants
errors.cause: A moving object and the reference are in one branch of the hierarchy.

tools.name: editor.plan_duplicates
tools.summary: Plans independent copies of an object and everything under it. Each copy gets fresh ids and an offset. It returns one scene.duplicate_hierarchy command.
when: To make a row, a grid or a stack of copies of a finished part.
For a row of new simple shapes, modeling.generate_commands is the alternative.

rows.name: sourceId
rows.meaning: The object to copy. Its descendants are copied with it.

rows.name: copies
rows.meaning: Additional copies.

rows.name: offset
rows.meaning: Within ±100000 per axis. Copy n moves by offset × n.

rows.name: space
rows.meaning: Whether the offset is in the parent's axes or in world axes.

rows.name: name
rows.meaning: A label for the copies' roots. Names are numbered among siblings when applied.
Propose with this as expectedRevision.
One scene.duplicate_hierarchy command with a new objectId for each root and each registered descendant.
Pass it to editor.propose_commands instead of the commands, so the generated ids are not copied by hand.
The next step.

response.nextAction: Call editor.propose_commands with this planId and apply true (no need to copy the generated ids), then inspect the copies.

flow: Read the hierarchy at the current revision
Generate fresh ids for each copy root and descendant
Propose it by planId with apply true
Inspect a copy

visual.caption: Top view. Copy n moves by [2.5, 0, 0] × n in world space.

tips: Copies are independent: geometry, materials and skeletons are separate. Texture images are shared.
Ids change on every call, so refer to copies by name after they are applied.
limits: The scene may hold 2000 objects, copies included. Geometry is budgeted at 128 MiB.
A skinned hierarchy must include all of its bones, or the copy is rejected.

errors.message: Update the editor for hierarchy duplication
errors.cause: The connected editor does not report supportsRepetition.

errors.message: Source object "…" does not exist; use an id from editor.get_context
errors.cause: sourceId is not in the scene.

errors.message: Copies exceed the 2000-object scene limit; make fewer copies
errors.cause: The copies would take the scene past 2000 objects.

tools.name: modeling.generate_commands
tools.summary: Runs a short JavaScript function in an isolated sandbox and returns the editor commands it calculates. Nothing is applied or proposed.
when: For layouts with arithmetic in them: a row, a ring, a grid, or a mesh built from computed vertices.
A direct scene.transform_object is simpler when the layout is simple.

rows.name: source
rows.meaning: The body of a synchronous function. Return an array of commands.

rows.name: inspection
rows.meaning: When given, the inspected mesh is passed as the second argument, mesh.

rows.label: scene
rows.meaning: A JSON snapshot: revision, objects, selectedObjectIds and world bounds.

rows.label: mesh
rows.meaning: The inspection, or null.

rows.label: Time
rows.meaning: 250 ms of run time.

rows.label: Memory and stack
rows.meaning: 16 MiB of heap, 256 KiB of stack.

rows.label: Output
rows.meaning: 256,000 characters. 1–200 commands with unique commandIds.

rows.label: Not available
rows.meaning: Imports, files, network, timers and asynchronous code.
sourceRevision, planId and commands, parsed by the strict command schema (defaults such as replaceExisting: false are filled in). Propose them by planId.
sourceRevision and issues (each with a commandId), or a message when the program failed.

flow: The assistant writes a function body
The sandbox runs it against a scene snapshot
Commands are parsed and checked against the scene
editor.propose_commands takes them by planId

visual.caption: Top view of the five create_primitive commands. Each box is 1 unit wide.

tips: Use a program when the layout has arithmetic or repetition. Use direct commands for one or two edits.
Use geometry.create_mesh for custom shapes: 3–4096 vertices, 1–4096 faces, and no more than 20,000 triangles.
limits: Nothing is proposed or applied. Pass the planId to editor.propose_commands, which carries sourceRevision as expectedRevision.
Material and texture commands cannot be generated. They need a separate proposal after editor.inspect_materials.

errors.message: The arguments do not match this tool's schema
errors.cause: The source is empty or longer than 16,000 characters, or the inspection request is invalid. issues names each field.

response.instructions:
# Mesh editing workflow

1. Call `editor.get_context` and confirm every target object exists.
2. Describe the change in plain language, then build the smallest set of commands that achieves it.
… (the rest of the workflow is in skills/mesh-editing/SKILL.md)
validation: Each target object id exists in the latest editor context.
Transforms use finite numbers, and scale values are positive.
Replacing geometry is an explicit destructive command and applies automatically through a proposal.
errorHandling: If a target object is missing, stop and ask the user which object to change.
If the user rejects a destructive proposal, do not retry it. Propose a non-destructive alternative instead.
Report revision conflicts, read the current context, and recalculate before proposing corrected commands.

tools.name: modeling.assess_quality
tools.summary: Records the independent reviewer's verdict on the finished work. Only the reviewer has this tool; the assistant that builds cannot grade itself.
when: Called by the quality reviewer, once, as its last step, after it has looked at the finished scene.
Never by the assistant that built the result. It receives the findings as work to do.

rows.name: outcome
rows.meaning: Whether the assistant sees no major defects, identifies work to do, or is blocked.

rows.name: summary
rows.meaning: Specific assessment or blocker.

rows.name: findings
rows.meaning: Each has aspect, observation, severity (major or minor) and optionally fix: what to change, up to 240 characters.

rows.label: ready
rows.meaning: ready needs pictures of two distinct live solid views the reviewer took at the current scene, observations on at least two distinct aspects, no major finding, and a measured, passing brief.

rows.label: blocked
rows.meaning: Explains an actual limitation with at least one finding and may be recorded without visual evidence.

rows.label: needs_refinement
rows.meaning: Needs at least one major finding. When pictures are possible the reviewer must have looked first; without pictures the findings may rest on measurements. Only minor findings mean ready, not a request for work.
Returns outcome, summary, findingCount and whether visual evidence was required.
Reason the review could not be recorded.

request.summary: Images are unavailable, so the shape cannot be visually assessed.

findings.observation: The model connection cannot receive images.

response.summary: Images are unavailable, so the shape cannot be visually assessed.

flow: The builder finishes its work
The reviewer captures distinct live views
The reviewer records its verdict
The builder fixes major findings; the result is reviewed again

visual.caption: A quality review is evidence for a revision, not a guarantee.

steps.title: Improve
steps.description: Fix significant issues and review again.

tips: Findings should say what is wrong, how serious it is, and what to change, so the builder can act on them.
A review that cannot judge records blocked and says what could not be checked; a reviewer that gives no verdict is recorded as blocked, never as approval.
limits: The verdict is a fallible judgment, but one made by an agent that did not build the result and starts with fresh context.
Candidate previews and measurement-only captures do not count as live visual evidence.
A scene revision change invalidates earlier visual evidence.

errors.message: A ready verdict needs pictures of at least two distinct live solid views taken after the latest change. If pictures are unavailable, record blocked and say the result was not visually verified.
errors.cause: ready was recorded without enough fresh image evidence.

tools.name: modeling.record_brief
tools.summary: Writes down what the finished work must be as checks that code can pass or fail: sizes, placement, symmetry and counts. Recording a brief changes nothing in the scene.
when: After reading the scene and before the plan, for any request that builds or reshapes something.
Whenever a request has a measurable meaning: real proportions, parts resting on what carries them, left and right matching, details inside their parent.
Skip it for a rename, a move or a question.

input.note: The brief is what the run is held to: it is not finished while a check fails.

rows.name: subject
rows.meaning: What is being made.

rows.name: style
rows.meaning: The look asked for, such as low poly or realistic.

rows.name: assumptions
rows.meaning: Choices made where the user gave no detail, such as the scale. They are for the user to read.

rows.name: checks
rows.meaning: Measurable statements about the finished scene. Each kind is described below.

rows.label: id
rows.meaning: The object's id.

rows.label: name
rows.meaning: Its exact name, ignoring letter case. Must match one object when the check is measured.

rows.label: namePrefix
rows.meaning: Names that start with this text, such as Leg for Leg, Leg.001 and Leg.002. Only the count check takes it.

rows.label: count
rows.meaning: How many objects match: at least min (default 1) and at most max.

rows.label: size
rows.meaning: The extent of target along axis, between min and max.

rows.label: position
rows.meaning: Where the low edge (min), middle (center) or high edge (max) of target lies on axis, between min and max. Lowest point on the floor: anchor min, min 0, max 0.

rows.label: gap
rows.meaning: From the high edge of first to the low edge of second along axis. 0 is touching, negative is overlapping.

rows.label: symmetric
rows.meaning: second mirrors first across the plane where axis equals planeAt (default 0), within tolerance.

rows.label: aligned
rows.meaning: first and second have the same center on axis, within tolerance.

rows.label: contained
rows.meaning: inner lies inside outer on every axis, within tolerance.

rows.label: connected
rows.meaning: Every mesh at or under group touches the rest, directly or through other parts, within tolerance (default 1% of the group's largest side). Names the parts that are detached. Touching means the bounds meet, which is necessary for contact but not proof of it.

rows.label: Bounds
rows.meaning: World-space axis-aligned bounds in scene units. A group's bounds include its parts, so name a whole thing by its group.

rows.label: tolerance
rows.meaning: Scene units. Left out, 2% of the largest side of the objects compared (1% for contained).

rows.label: label
rows.meaning: Optional name for a check, up to 120 characters, shown in results.
checkCount, replaced and next. A warning appears when a brief with failing checks was replaced.

request.subject: A figure with two matching arms, standing beside a crate
assumptions: One scene unit is one meter
The figure is about as tall as a person

checks.label: Figure is about as tall as a person

response.next: Build the model, then call validation.check_brief after the changes are applied.

visual.caption: Four checks for the sample scene, each one a number the code can test.

groups.title: Symmetry
items: arm_left and arm_right mirror each other across x

tips: Write checks for what makes this subject right, not for what is easy to pass.
Name objects the way the plan will create them. The objects need not exist when the brief is recorded.
Recording again replaces the brief. The user is told at the end how many times it changed, so change a check only when it was wrong.
limits: Checks measure bounds, so they prove sizes, placement, mirroring and that parts meet, but not shape or appearance.
Bounds are axis-aligned boxes: a turned part can fail a size check that its true shape would pass.
An editor that does not report bounds leaves the checks unmeasurable; the final reply says so.

errors.message: Give exactly one of id, name or namePrefix
errors.cause: A check named an object in more than one way, or in none.

errors.message: namePrefix is only for count checks; use id or name
errors.cause: A size, position, gap, symmetric, aligned or contained check pointed at several objects.

tools.name: validation.check_brief
tools.summary: Measures the recorded brief against the current scene and reports each check as pass, fail or unresolved, with what was measured and what was needed.
when: After applying changes, as the step that follows validation.check_scene.
Again after every fix, until no check fails. The run is not finished while a check fails or the scene changed since the last measurement.

input.note: No input. Send an empty object.

rows.meaning: pass, fail, unmeasurable (the editor sent no bounds) or rejected (no brief recorded).
The scene revision that was measured.
Counts of checks.
For each check: index, label, kind, status, measured and expected.

rows.label: pass
rows.meaning: The measured value is inside what the check needs.

rows.label: fail
rows.meaning: The model is wrong or the check was. measured and expected show by how much.

rows.label: unresolved
rows.meaning: The check could not be measured: the object does not exist yet, several objects have that name, or it has no geometry. measured says which.

results.label: Figure is about as tall as a person

visual.caption: Result for the sample scene: the figure floats 0.25 above the floor.

groups.title: Pass
items: Figure is about as tall as a person: 1.55
Arms mirror each other: exact mirror

groups.title: Fail
items: Figure stands on the floor: 0.25, needs exactly 0

tips: Fix every fail and unresolved check, then measure again. Do not loosen a check to make it pass unless it was wrong, and say so in the reply.
A passing brief is not a finished model. Look at the scene with viewport.capture for shape and appearance.
limits: It reads the snapshot only and cannot find parts that overlap without being listed in a check.
Only changes the run applied are tracked: a change made by the user in between is measured the next time it runs.
